source: The year-to-year coefficient of variation of the harvest by region (W29): v1's twelve-region referee table (tools/probe_yieldcv.mjs, docs/harvest-years-2026-08-25.md), the approximate pre-modern bands drawn from FAO yield-variability studies and the historical famine literature named per region. A region is the land inside its box [lonMin, lonMax, latMin, latMax]; the check is the fertility-weighted median of the static yield CV over the box's land cells with fertility above fertilityFloor, at both grids, from the substrate alone (no history is simulated).
statistic: fertility-weighted median over land cells with fertility > fertilityFloor

regions.name: England and northern France
regions.source: Maritime temperate rain-fed grain: Hoskins 1964/1968 (harvest fluctuations, England 1480-1759), Campbell 2007 (medieval demesne yields); the reliably-watered floor

regions.name: Mediterranean Spain
regions.source: Winter-rain dry farming, the summer-dry season on a thin margin

regions.name: Greece and the Aegean
regions.source: Gallant 1991 (Risk and Survival in Ancient Greece: interannual wheat and barley variability); Garnsey 1988

regions.name: The Sahel
regions.source: Rain-fed millet at the desert margin on one short season: Sivakumar 1988 (Sahelian rainfall and crop variability); chronic famine (Watts 1983)

regions.name: The Nile valley
regions.source: The flood regime: Hassan 1981 (historical Nile floods), Butzer 1976 (Early Hydraulic Civilization in Egypt); the pre-dam bad-flood years

regions.name: Mesopotamia
regions.source: Irrigated alluvium under a desert sky: Adams 1981 (Heartland of Cities); the Tigris-Euphrates flood and salt variability

regions.name: The Ganges plain
regions.source: Monsoon rice and wheat on a wet plain with a river: Parthasarathy et al. 1988 (monsoon rainfall and grain), the Bengal famine literature

regions.name: The North China plain
regions.source: A monsoon that stacks the rain in the warm half over a cold winter, with the Yellow River's floods: Will 1990 (Bureaucracy and Famine in Eighteenth-Century China), Elvin 2004

regions.name: The Pontic steppe
regions.source: Continental dryland wheat: Wheatcroft 1977 (Russian grain yields), the Don and Kuban dryland bands; the box is the steppe belt, not the forest-steppe north of it

regions.name: The Kazakh steppe
regions.source: The Virgin Lands' recorded yield swings (McCauley 1976); a −8 °C cool half over a thin margin

regions.name: Java and the wet tropics
regions.source: Wet-tropical rice with rain in every month: the lowest interannual variability of any staple region (Boomgaard 1989)

regions.name: The south Indian interior
regions.source: The semi-arid Deccan on a short monsoon: Guhathakurta & Rajeevan 2008 (rainfall variability), the Deccan famine record (Bhatia 1967)
